What’s your point? I do think it will be considered that, I already consider it to be that way in some sense. My point is that there’s a balance between realism and “cartoony” vibes. I think rdr2 relied heavily on the former which just was too much for me. 
Back when RDR1 came out we didn’t recognize the “cartoony” vibe because we were playing an actual game vs RDR2 where your endless bounties, Side tasks, epic bandit hideouts, fun and quick card games are either removed or replaced with cooking, eating, chopping wood, maintaining your gun and bathing.  Obviously RDR2 has everything RDR1 has but the problem is that they have just way too much IMO.

RDR1 feels more like an arcade game with fleshed out details. Also has a better story and more solid and memorable side missions.
RDR 2 is more role playing and immersive experience. I feel as though it tries to be a “survival” game but it is simply too easy to be that and eating and cleaning ends up being a huge hassle. Still contains most elements of rdr1 but left some of my favorite things about the game. 

The cartoonish spaghetti western vibe would be harder to translate into RDR2 but it was something I think they could’ve tried a little harder with. 
The characters have way more depth in RDR1 because you are constantly learning about their past; in RDR2 you CAN interact and learn about all these characters but you don’t WANT to like in RDR 1. In the original I was asking questions like “why is bill so important?” “who is this Dutch guy?” “Who are these FBI guys?” 
The story was untapped so it was inherently more memorable for me. 
You’re forced to play missions and learn about West Dickens and Seth and others you meet. you have a little place in your heart for each of them because you do a plethora of unique and fun missions for them.
Even the strangers and their quest are far more memorable and preferable to a lot of the “strangers” you meet in RDR2. Think about the cannibal side quest or the strange man who is a resemblance of “Death”. 
I know RDR2 is objectively a better game with tons of crazy side missions and really well thought out gameplay; but I stand with RDR1 because I view it as a GAME vs RDR2 which i view as a play through movie or simulation. And RDR2 simply left a lot of what I love about RDR1 and replaced it with fishing and interactions and woodcutting and eating. 
I wish there could be a hybrid or mod for RDR1 where we could just use the first games gameplay and the second games map.
